text.title: Lean Stack Bootstrapper Blueprint Core Rules
text.summary: 6 testable rules every application of lean-stack-bootstrapper-blueprint enforces. Each rule has a statement, a rationale anchored to industry practice, and a source citation.

rule.statement: Stack has ≤5 services: Vercel (hosting+edge), Supabase (DB+auth+storage), Stripe (payments), Cloudflare (DNS+CDN+email forward), one observability (BetterStack / Sentry).
rule.rationale: ≤5 services keeps cognitive load + cost manageable; >5 = monitoring burden exceeds value.

rule.statement: Set a monthly cost ceiling ($50, $200, $500). Alert at 80%. Auto-pause non-essential at 100%.
rule.rationale: Lean stack autoscales; without ceiling, accidental run-up burns cash before next sale.

rule.statement: Do NOT introduce Docker, Kubernetes, or self-hosted services before the lean stack hits a real bottleneck.
rule.rationale: Premature container/k8s is the #1 indie-hacker time sink; lean stack covers 90% of first-year needs.

rule.statement: Accept vendor lock-in as a feature. Free tier's job is shipping, not portability. Optimize portability after PMF.
rule.rationale: Portability obsession kills shipping cadence; pre-PMF, vendor lock-in is a feature.

rule.statement: Document triggers to graduate: monthly cost > 30% of MRR, p95 latency > 1s, vendor outage > 4h/month. Otherwise stay lean.
rule.rationale: Explicit triggers prevent both premature scaling + denial of legitimate scaling needs.

rule.statement: When the team has a DevOps engineer who prefers k8s / IaC, or a compliance constraint (HIPAA, SOC 2) requires self-hosted infrastructure, the blueprint MUST NOT be applied: the agent MUST NOT produce the <=5-service Vercel + Supabase + Stripe + Cloudflare diagram, the monthly ceiling or the vendor-lock acceptance note for that team, and MUST route to the Pro-tier Docker / k8s / CI/CD infrastructure methodologies. The skip MUST name which exit fired - `graduate-to-pro-stack` for the DevOps case, `not-applicable` for the compliance case - so r3 (no premature Docker) is not later cited against a team that was never in scope.

rationale.source: HHS HIPAA Security Rule; AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria; practitioner experience

rule.rationale: r3 and r4 are correct only when nobody on the team can run infrastructure and nothing forces them to; a DevOps hire or a self-hosting mandate falsifies both premises. Applying the lean rules anyway either wastes the engineer or ships a stack the audit rejects, and the two exits differ in what comes next: one is a graduation, the other was never a fit.
